chunks: And from him, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) in Kufa and said: 'I have divorced my wife after she had become pure from her menses, before I had intercourse with her.'
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Did you bear witness with two just men, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded you?'
He said: 'No.' He said: 'Go, for your divorce is not valid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a valid divorce in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *shuhud* (witnessing) as a condition for the validity of divorce, not merely its notification. Imam Ali (peace be upon him) links the procedural requirement of two just witnesses directly to the divine command, ruling that the absence of witnesses renders the divorce null (*laysa bi-shay'*). This reflects the Shia juristic view that divorce is a formal legal act requiring public verification to prevent secret or disputed separations.
